subject: Dedicated commit sizing: ZenBridge throughput / latency runway analysis
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@zenbridge.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated commit sizing: initial numbers and ask

Elena — thanks for the time earlier. Per our discovery, I want to capture the concrete numbers so we can size a Dedicated commit that meets your p95 latency SLO and gives reasonable headroom during your expected peaks. Attaching a quick estimator (zenbridge_tokens_model_estimate.xlsx) that shows the inputs below.

Summary (please confirm):
- Target model for pilot: redwood-codex-30B (fp16) — you also mentioned evaluating quantized variants later.
- Average user request length (prompt + expected generated tokens): 170 tokens
- Expected steady request rate: 50 reqs/sec
- Expected peak multiplier (business hours bursts): 3.5x
- p95 latency target: 350 ms end-to-end (network + inference)
- KV/prefix cache potential: ~15% effective token reduction for repeated prefixes (we should test)

Key asks for engineering sizing:
1) Can you confirm the model variant we should use for the SLA measurement (fp16 vs int8)?
2) Any constraint on cold-starts / acceptable queuing during peak (max queued requests)?
3) Do you want us to include a canary window with a smaller committed slab (recommended) before full commit?

Initial ask: please review the attached estimator and confirm the average tokens/req and peak multiplier. Once confirmed, Ben will run a performance pass against our fleet and propose a recommended slab with headroom and fallback variants.

Thanks,
Mina
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: zenbridge_tokens_model_estimate.xlsx, redwood_sla_draft.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@zenbridge.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing: initial numbers and ask

Elena / Mina — I ran a quick perf sweep in our lab using the inputs Mina listed and a traffic profile that matches a 3.5x burst. Below are the relevant calculations and an initial recommendation. I attached the microbenchmark outputs to the estimator for traceability.

Raw numbers used (lab):
- Model: redwood-codex-30B (fp16, baseline kernel set)
- Measured sustained throughput per A100-equivalent GPU (p95, with dynamic batching and 64-token step warmup): ~8,000 tokens/sec
- Measured throughput for int8-quantized path (when warmed and with optimized kernels): ~12,000 tokens/sec (note: quality tradeoffs to validate)

Sizing math (simple):
- steady_tokens/sec = 50 reqs/sec * 170 tokens = 8,500 tokens/sec
- peak_tokens/sec = steady_tokens/sec * 3.5 = 29,750 tokens/sec
- GPUs_needed_fp16 = ceil(29,750 / 8,000) = 4 GPUs
- Add 30% headroom for p95 slos, noisy neighbors and orchestration jitter: 4 * 1.3 = 5.2 -> recommend 6 GPUs committed for SLA

Notes and rationale:
- We prefer rounding up to an even slab to allow token-bucket gating and least-disruptive failover (commit 6, canary commit 3).
- If you are comfortable validating quantized quality, int8 path reduces GPUs_needed to ceil(29,750 / 12,000) = 3 -> with 30% headroom -> 4 GPUs. That is a lower-cost commit but requires eval on your prompt set before we can include it in an SLA.
- KV/prefix cache: assuming you get ~15% effective token reduction for repeated prefixes, effective peak drops to ~25,287 tokens/sec -> reduces GPUs_needed by one in fp16 case (still recommend 5 committed + 1 buffer). We should run your sample workload to quantify.
- Tail latency: to keep p95 < 350ms we must limit batching windows and bound queue lengths. Operationally we enforce a max batch latency of 30ms and backpressure at route-level for spikes beyond committed slab.

Operational recommendations:
- Canary: 3-GPU canary for 2 weeks; validate end-to-end p95s and quality on production samples.
- Rollout plan: 3 -> 4 -> 6 over 6 weeks tied to usage thresholds (we can automate).
- Fallbacks: deploy int8 variant as an alternate route; automatic fallback when latency or queueing breaches thresholds.
- Autoscale for burst absorb (soft): allow 1-2 GPU burst capacity on dedicated pool for short lived peaks (billing/commit implications to discuss).

Estimated cost delta between fp16 6-GPU commit vs int8 4-GPU commit is ~28% on our current pricing model. We can provide exact numbers in the proposal doc.

Next steps: Mina — if Elena confirms model quality acceptance criteria, I’ll schedule a 48-hr perf run against a sanitized sample of production prompts and return a final slab recommendation and runbook.

—Ben
Principal Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@zenbridge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Mar 2028 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing: initial numbers and ask

Thanks Ben — this helps a lot. Quick clarifications from our side:
- We'll validate int8 on a holdout set; quality bar is max mean token-level perplexity delta of 2.0 vs fp16 and no visible hallucination regressions on our 200 eval prompts.
- Cache: ~40% of inbound requests share the same prompt prefix; if caching removes repeated prefixes at token-level we expect close to the 15% reduction you mentioned but would like Redwood to validate against our dataset.
- Billing/pilot: we prefer a 4-week canary (not 2) with a reduced committed slab and a 2-week evaluation window before full commit. During the canary, can Redwood apply trial credits to offset the burst GPU usage that exceeds the canary slab?

Also — can you confirm whether cold-start penalties will be an issue for our use case? We have some low-frequency admins that trigger large-generation flows intermittently.

Thanks,
Elena
CTO, ZenBridge
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@zenbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Mar 2028 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing: initial numbers and ask

Elena — agreed on the longer canary. Confirming next steps and decisions: 

1) Canary plan: 4-week canary on a 3-GPU slab (commit: 3 GPUs reserved) with trial credits applied to any burst capacity used beyond the 3 GPUs for the duration of the canary. We'll capture overage during the canary and discount it as a one-time credit when you convert to full commit (documented in the SLA draft attached).
2) Perf validation: Ben will run a 72-hr perf sweep against your sanitized sample (we'll need the sample upload link). He'll report both fp16 and int8 numbers, and include perplexity/quality delta for the holdout prompts.
3) Cold starts: operationally we keep a warm pool for infrequent warm-up flows (configurable). Cold start penalties can be limited by keeping a small warm standby; we'll add a recommendation in the runbook.
4) Timeline: perf run starts Mon 13 Mar if you can share the sanitized prompts by EOD Sun. We’ll aim to deliver the final slab recommendation and a canary runbook (runbook_canary_steps.md) by Wed 15 Mar.

Action items:
- ZenBridge: upload sanitized sample to https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bZenBridgeRunbook by EOD Sun (Elena / Marco)
- Redwood: Ben will start perf tests and Mina will send an updated commercial with the trial-credit clause.
- DocuSign: I’ve attached the current SLA draft; I’ll also push a DocuSign link once the commercial terms are finalized.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the 13 Mar kickoff.

Best,
Mina
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
